speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your newborn check-up. I see there is some unverified data provided, but I will rely on my clinical examination and your answers. To begin, how old is the baby in hours, and have you noticed any skin discoloration, particularly a bluish tint to the lips or extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus or E. coli) in a newborn with no prenatal care and unknown immunization status. The absence of prenatal care and lack of immunization records are significant risk factors for severe bacterial infection, even in the absence of overt skin discoloration yet. Please confirm the baby's current temperature, feeding status, and whether there is any respiratory distress such as grunting or retractions. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and blood culture; REQUEST TEST: Gram stain of blood; REQUEST TEST: C-reactive protein (CRP).
